mission: Steinhardt (associate professor of Statistics and EECS, part of BAIR) studies why ML systems produce unintended consequences — e.g. exploiting reward errors in ways that get worse as models grow — and builds tools to understand models' internal activations and to let AI help humans understand complex systems. He also founded and leads the nonprofit Transluce. Founding year approximate (joined Berkeley faculty ~2019).

key_work.title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
key_work.plain_summary: Landmark agenda (with Amodei, Olah and others) naming practical accident risks: side effects, reward hacking, scalable oversight, safe exploration, distribution shift.

key_work.title: Unsolved Problems in ML Safety
key_work.plain_summary: Updated agenda (with Hendrycks, Carlini, Schulman) organising safety into robustness, monitoring, alignment and systemic safety.

key_work.title: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU)
key_work.plain_summary: The 57-subject benchmark that became a standard yardstick of AI knowledge.

key_work.title: Jailbroken: How Does LLM Safety Training Fail?
key_work.plain_summary: Explains jailbreaks via two failure modes — competing objectives and mismatched generalisation — and shows they defeat safety training.

key_work.title: Discovering Latent Knowledge in Language Models Without Supervision
key_work.plain_summary: Finds a 'truth direction' in model activations that can reveal what a model 'knows' even when its output is wrong.

people.role: Associate professor; founder & CEO of Transluce

warnings.text: ML systems tend to exploit errors in the reward function, and this unintended behaviour often gets worse as models get bigger (site).
Problems compound when ML systems interact with each other or with humans, creating strategic incentives (site).

recommendations.text: Understand models' latent activations, not just outputs, so their computation can be modified to fit human intent.
Use AI to help humans understand complex systems and forecast long-term consequences.
